A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sharpness disparity principle and Blockwise LR method. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2/LLaMA training results, sharpness measurements, block ablations, learning-rate sensitivity experiments, and Adam-mini comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds larger-model and C4 results, downstream task evaluations, and Lion/WSD experiments.

M1.justification: The block grouping, sharpness estimator, learning-rate adjustment rule, default ratios, and switch after warmup remain unchanged. Lion and WSD experiments apply the existing strategy without introducing a new Blockwise LR component or adjustment procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds C4 pre-training alongside OpenWebText and MiniPile. It also introduces downstream evaluations on ARC-E, ARC-C, PIQA, HellaSwag, OBQA, WinoGrande, and SCIQ, substantially extending coverage beyond pre-training loss and sharpness measurements.

E2.justification: Lion becomes an evaluated comparator in v2 Figure 7, which compares vanilla Lion with Lion using Blockwise LR. The existing AdamW and Adam-mini comparisons remain; the comparator expansion is limited to this additional optimizer.

E3.justification: Existing OpenWebText/MiniPile protocols are retained. New settings include a 2B model, C4 training with sequence length 256, batch size 512 and approximately 20 training tokens per parameter, and zero-shot downstream evaluation using lm-evaluation-harness. Appendix A.3 additionally specifies Lion tuning and a WSD schedule with a stable phase through 66.7% of training followed by decay to zero.

E4.justification: v2 adds an explicit comparison of benefits across model scales in Figure 5, optimizer/scheduler robustness experiments with Lion and WSD in Figure 7, and sharpness evolution under Lion in Figure 11. These substantially extend the original block ablations, ratio sensitivity, and layer/parameter analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces no new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures. Additional performance results retain the existing point-result reporting approach.

E6.justification: v2 adds 2B and C4 loss results, Lion/WSD outcomes, and seven downstream comparisons. The new 2B panel reports a 2.31× speedup; new Table 1 reports WinoGrande scores of 55.17 for AdamW versus 59.83 for Blockwise LR. These are additional experiments, not revised v1 measurements. The original ablation values remain unchanged in v2 Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, sharpness estimator, Theorems 4.1–4.3, and their complete Appendix B proofs are substantively unchanged. The new empirical scaling comparisons introduce no additional theorem or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the demonstrated acceleration scope from models up to 1.1B on two datasets to models up to 2B with C4 included. The central sharpness ordering, Blockwise LR contribution, near-2× acceleration claim, and Adam-mini memory-saving claim remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 newly interprets widening performance gaps on MiniPile/OpenWebText and approximately parallel C4 curves as suggesting benefits may persist at larger scales. It also connects lower pre-training loss with downstream usefulness. Existing mechanism explanations and future-work limitations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies a project-code link and substantially expands reproducibility documentation: 2B/C4 architecture and learning-rate tables, the C4 tokenizer and token budget, Lion learning-rate/weight-decay tuning, and WSD timing. Original hardware and retained experiment settings remain documented; the additions principally specify the new experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Raffel et al. for C4/T5, Hoffmann et al. for compute-optimal training budgets, and Zhao et al.'s optimizer study for experimental settings. The positioning relative to earlier Hessian analyses and optimization methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 expands Section 6.1, broadens the headings and content of Section 6.3 and Appendix A.3, adds an Impact Statement, removes the appendix contents list, and updates publication and affiliation text.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, extensively resizing and repositioning displays. It adds scaling, Lion/WSD, and Lion-sharpness figures plus downstream and C4 tables. Figure 4 replaces its duplicated 1.1B panel with a 2B panel; the 1.1B result remains in Figure 1.

improvement.justification: v1 demonstrated pre-training loss improvements without testing downstream usefulness or an alternative learning-rate schedule. v2 addresses these substantive validation gaps through seven downstream tasks and Lion/WSD experiments, while adding C4, larger-model evidence, and reproducibility information. These additions substantially strengthen evidence of practical utility and generality. Run-to-run uncertainty remains unreported, but the retained method, proofs, and original results are not weakened.
